The matter is being taken up through Video Conferencing.
Learned counsel for the parties have no objection with it and submitted that audio and video qualities are good.

Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company, Mr. Alok Lal has submitted, that I.A. No.5908 of 2021 has been filed to delete the name of respondent no.4, namely,
Bimla Devi, W/o Late Sambhu Nath Agrawal.
Considering the reasons assigned in the Interlocutory Application, I.A. No.5908 of 2021 is allowed.
Office is directed to delete the name of respondent no.4, namely, Bimla Devi from memo of appeal.

Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company, Mr. Alok Lal has assailed the impugned award dated 08.06.2018 passed by learned District Judge-II-cum-Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal, Bokaro in Motor Accident claim Case No.05 of 2014 whereby the claimants, namely, 1.
Suman Agrawal, 2. Sourabh Agrawal, 3. Komal Agrawal and 4. Bimla Devi, who died during pendency of the appeal and her name has been deleted vide I.A. No.5908 of 2021, have been Divisional Manager vs Suman Agrawal on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79846965/
1 awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.57,64,812/- along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application dated 15.01.2014 to be indemnified within 90 days, failing which, the interest shall be 9% per annum.
Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company, Mr. Alok Lal has assailed the impugned award on the ground that on the alleged date of occurrence i.e. 27.07.2013, the motorcycle bearing Registration No.JH-09C- 6911 was driven by Sunil Kumar Agrawal and deceased, Dilip Kumar Agrawal, who was a pillion rider, fell down from the motorcycle and sustained injuries.

sentences.text: He was brought to Neelam Hospital with the help of the local people, where he died during treatment.
Thereafter F.I.R. was registered as U.D. Case No.10 of 2013 and after investigation the final form was submitted on the same day i.e. 27.07.2013.

The Sub-Divisional Officer has dropped the proceeding vide order dated 05.09.2013, which have been brought on record as Exhibits-6 and 7 respectively and the learned Tribunal has not considered the same.

Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company, Mr. Alok Lal has submitted, that claim application was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, but it is sine qua non for the same to prove rash and negligent driving, otherwise the application could have been maintainable under Section 163-A of the MV Act, as such, impugned award is bad in law and may be set aside.

Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company, Mr. Alok Lal has relied upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Premlata Shukla, reported in (2007) 13 SCC 476 and in the case of Surender Kumar Arora & Anr. vs. Dr.
Manoj Bisla & Ors. reported in 2012 (4) SCC 552.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company, Mr. Alok Lal has submitted, that it is the duty of owner of the offending vehicle to produce the driving licence of the driver, which has not been produced, as such, liability cannot be fastened upon the Insurance Company rather there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy because of the non- co- operation of the owner of the offending vehicle.
Learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants, Mr. Nikhil Ranjan has submitted, that no such plea was taken by the Insurance Company before the learned Tribunal.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Chamundeswari and others reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 849

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , has categorically held that if any evidence before the Tribunal runs contrary to the contents in the First Information Report, the evidence which is recorded before the Tribunal has to be given weightage over the contents of the First Information Report.

Learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants, Mr. Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted,
that the case of Premlata Shukla (supra) has already been considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Chamundeswari and others (Supra).
Learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants, Mr. Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted,
that even the issue has not been framed nor any cross-examination has been made by the Insurance Company nor the Insurance Company has brought any evidence on record to establish that there Divisional Manager vs Suman Agrawal on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79846965/
2 was rash and negligent driving by the Sunil Kumar Agrawal, Motorcycle bearing Registration No.JH-09C-6911 insured before the United India Insurance Company Limited on relevant day dated 27.07.2013 vide Insurance Policy No.2107013113P100835890 valid for the period from 10.05.2013 to 09.05.2014.
Learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants, Mr. Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted,
that whatever the issues are being raised before this Court those have never been raised before the learned Tribunal nor such issue was framed nor any evidence has been brought on record by the appellant contrary to the evidence of the claimants, as such, impugned award does not suffer from illegality or irregularity and does not require any interference by this Court as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Nirmala Kothari vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd., reported in 2020 (4) SCC 49.
Learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 to 3/claimants, Mr. Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted,
that the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Surender Kumar Arora (Supra) is not applicable in the present facts and circumstances of the case as no contrary evidence has been brought on record by the Insurance Company to deny the averments and evidence brought on record by the claimants, that the deceased- Dilip Kumar Agrawal has not died because of the rash and negligent driving by the Sunil Kumar Agrawal, as such, the appellant has no case and the instant Miscellaneous Appeal may be dismissed.

entities.text: Nirmala Kothari vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd., reported in 2020 (4) SCC 49
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties, perused the impugned award as well as the judgment relied upon by the learned counsel for the parties.
This Court is of the opinion that the Insurance Company has not pleaded all these issues before the learned Tribunal and they are raising these issues before the appellate court.

It appears that no issue was framed with regard to the motorcycle driven by another person, Sunil Kumar Agrawal before the learned Tribunal rather the learned Tribunal has decided that the driver of the offending motorcycle had valid driving licence at the time of accident while deciding issue no.4, as such, no discrepancy or irregularity is there in the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal.

The learned Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence brought in the claim case as no contrary evidence has been brought on record by the Insurance Company,
accordingly, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.
The instant Miscellaneous Appeal is hereby dismissed.
Interim order granted vide order dated 21.02.2019 stands vacated.
The awarded amount along with interest shall be paid in the nationalized bank account of the claimants.

The learned counsel for the claimants is directed to furnished the account number of the claimants of any nationalized bank to learned counsel for the Insurance Company or the learned Tribunal /
Executing Court within a period of two weeks.

It is expected that the Insurance Company shall indemnify the award within a period of 60 days along with interest from the date of filing of the claim application.
Divisional Manager vs Suman Agrawal on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79846965/
3

The statutory amount deposited by the Insurance Company shall be remitted to the learned Tribunal / Executing Court so as to indemnify the award to the claimants and if it is in excess of the awarded amount paid by the Insurance Company, the same shall be returned to the Insurance Company.
Let the Lower Court Records be sent back to the learned Court below.

(Kailash Prasad Deo, J.) R.S./
